correctness.rationale: The published normalized conditional Gaussian stationary law yields the exact finite-N maximum CDF. Normal extreme centering with the logarithmic correction yields fixed-shift Gumbel limits. Changing the environmental variable by w=(log N)u and w=(log N)(1-u) extracts the two endpoint powers and constants. Gaussian hazard-ratio inequalities give integrable doubly exponential or exponential dominators and control remote sectors. Separate Mills-ratio threshold sandwiches establish the nominal lower support leakage, and a normal-tail expansion establishes the extra inverse-square-root logarithm for upper support exceedances. The same bounds prove conditional-environment convergence. The standalone exact-mixture quadrature comparison produced 123 passing diagnostics; it is not substituted for infinite-N proof. Boundary assumptions and nonuniformities are explicit.

value.rationale: The motivating model has a surprising compactly supported leading distribution for a spatial extreme, yet at any finite particle number its maximum lies outside this compact support with positive probability. This theorem quantifies both boundary events with sharp and generally different log-particle powers, a lower loglog enhancement, an upper inverse-square-root-log penalty, crossover profiles and conditioned trap-variance laws, a two-scale refinement invisible to the known bulk weak limit. These are directly motivated finite-population edge observables rather than arbitrary parameter slices or a routine table recomputation; generality includes every positive switching-rate and stiffness pair.
